full_judgment: 8. Similarly in the above quoted second and third expressions we are not permitted in law to read them as "if an application for such revival is made by the Government to the Court, where proceedings were pending on the date they were deemed to have been stopped, within 90 days from that date" in place of the legislature's actual expression, "if an application for such revival is made by the Government to the Court, such proceedings were pending on the date they were stopped, within 90 days from that date". By using the said second and third expression in an unambiguous manner and in clear terms the legislature has left absolutely no doubt that the limitation of 90 days regarding making an application by the Government to the Court for revival of such case shall run from the date on which the Court concerned actually stopped the proceedings in respect of the trial of the case and not from the date on which the proceedings of the trial of the case should have been stopped or should be deemed to have been stopped.
